..(Tuesday night through Sunday)
Issued at 310 AM EST MON NOV 23 2026

The extended portion of the forecast appears to be on track for an
amplifying weather system moving through during the Holiday. This
appears to bring cold soaking rains and breezy conditions to 
eastern Kentucky from late Wednesday through Thanksgiving night 
into the start of Black Friday. We continue to monitor the
potential for the overall system to be stronger and provide an
opportunity for some snow on its back end, though it still seems
unlikely with the latest model runs. The rest of the weekend will
dry out but another system looks to bring more rain to the area 
by Monday with mild conditions the rule into the start of 
December. 

The previous long term discussion follows:

The 22/12Z model suite analysis beginning Tuesday morning shows
shortwave ridging aloft extending from the Tennessee Valley to near
Lake Winnipeg, with an ~1037 mb surface high centered over the 
Driftless region. Anticyclonic flow around the high will be 
feeding a chilly air mass (925 hPa temperatures near 0C) on low- 
level northerly flow. Meanwhile, further upstream, three 500 hPa 
shortwaves/vort maxes are noted: one over the Southern High 
Plains, a second crossing southern Saskatchewan, and a third over 
the western Gulf of America.

The model suite is in good agreement showing the shortwave ridging
aloft propagating east of the JKL CWA during the day on Tuesday
while the attendant surface high scoots to over the Mid-Atlantic.
The southern stream shortwave will then dig along the Gulf Coast 
Tuesday night and Wednesday, sending moisture streaming northward 
across much of the Southeast CONUS while a weak area of low 
pressure initially takes shape in the vicinity of western Cuba 
before tracking toward the Florida Peninsula. Meanwhile, the 
northern-stream trough/closed low races southeast toward the Mid- 
Mississippi Valley. From Wednesday night through Friday, these 
three upper-level features phase to form a potentially sub-540 dam
closed low tracking up the Appalachians, mirrored at the surface 
by a strong Nor'easter slamming much of the East Coast with 
powerful winds and heavy rainfall.

Eastern Kentucky will be on the cold side of this developing low 
pressure system, but the available cold air is limited in its 
intensity. LREF mean 850 hPa temperatures are not far from 0C in 
the coldest air behind the low (though it is notable that this is 
a downward trend from prior model suites). At this point, 
thicknesses and atmospheric sounding profiles suggest temperatures
will be just a little too warm for snow, though a few flakes 
mixing in cannot be ruled out. This will need to be monitored 
closely, as further cooling in the guidance could yield more 
flakiness than currently anticipated. Overall, this system is
presently favored to yield a miserably raw period of intermittent
rainfall for the Thanksgiving holiday as well as the bracketing 
nighttime periods. Rainfall amount forecasts continue to increase,
with widespread 0.25 to 0.50 inch amounts now favored and 
significantly more (1 to 2 inches) possible in wetter scenarios. 
Once the precipitation departs, heights rebound across eastern 
Kentucky briefly next weekend as surface high pressure passes 
across the Southeast US. The resulting southwesterly flow should 
allow for a temporary rebound in temperatures to above-normal 
levels.

In sensible terms, look for a characteristically chilly November
Tuesday with highs in the mid 40s to near 50F, accompanied by a
weak northerly breeze and mostly clear skies. Temperatures dip 
back to near freezing on Tuesday night before clouds increase on 
Wednesday, along with late-day rain chances. Temperatures could 
rebound into the 50s on Wednesday ahead of the arrival of 
precipitation. Conditions then turn rainy and raw from late 
Wednesday through Thursday night with temperatures in the 30s to 
around 40F at night and probably only in the 40s on Thursday. A 
few flakes cannot be ruled out, especially as precipitation ends 
Thursday night. Dry conditions and a gradual warming trend follow 
for next weekend with highs in the 40s on Friday, lower to mid 50s
on Saturday, and well into the 50s to perhaps nearing 60F in the 
warmest spots on Sunday.
